# Configuration reference

The gateway reads one configuration file, `config.yaml` in this documentation, when it starts: `slay400-gateway run --config config.yaml`. It is YAML, at most 1 MiB, in UTF-8. The gateway checks the whole file before it listens, reports every problem with its line and column and a code from GWY001 to GWY009 or GWY015, and does not start while one is left; `slay400-gateway check --config config.yaml` does the same and exits. A change to the file takes effect at the next start; bundles and certificate files are taken without a restart (see `reload`).

A value can be, or contain, a `${NAME}` placeholder: the gateway puts in the value of the environment variable `NAME` at start, and stops with GWY007 if it is not set. Credentials and the key password must be exactly one placeholder (GWY015): a value written in the file is refused.

## server

The API listener serves the operations at `/<tenant>/<environment>/<route>` and the health checks `/health/live` and `/health/ready`, never `/metrics`. Earlier development builds named its address `server.host`; that key is now refused with GWY002 and a message that names `server.address`.

With `server.tls`, a certificate or key that is missing, unreadable, not PEM, not matching each other, expired or not valid yet stops the start (GWY022 to GWY024); a certificate that expires within 30 days is a warning (GWY025). The two files are polled every `reload.intervalSeconds` and a new pair is used for new connections.

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Limits | A change takes effect | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `server` | section | no |  |  | at a restart | The API listener: it serves the operations and the health checks. |
| `server.address` | text | no | `127.0.0.1` | no white space | at a restart | The address the API listener listens on; 0.0.0.0 for every address. |
| `server.port` | whole number | no | `8080` | 1 to 65535 | at a restart | The port of the API listener. |
| `server.tls` | section | no |  |  | at a restart | With this section the API listener speaks HTTPS only, TLS 1.3 and 1.2; without it, plain HTTP. |
| `server.tls.certificate` | file name | with server.tls |  | PEM: the certificate, then its chain | at a restart | The certificate of the API listener, relative to the configuration file. |
| `server.tls.key` | file name | with server.tls |  | PEM, PKCS#8 | at a restart | The private key of the certificate, relative to the configuration file. |
| `server.tls.keyPassword` | placeholder | for an encrypted key |  | a single ${NAME} | at a restart | The environment variable that holds the password of an encrypted key. |

## management

The management listener speaks plain HTTP and serves `/health/live`, `/health/ready` and `/metrics`. Keep it on an address that only your monitoring reaches.

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Limits | A change takes effect | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `management` | section | no |  |  | at a restart | The management listener, plain HTTP: health checks and metrics, never an operation. |
| `management.address` | text | no | `127.0.0.1` | no white space | at a restart | The address the management listener listens on. |
| `management.port` | whole number | no | `9090` | 0 to 65535; 0 turns the listener off | at a restart | The port of the management listener. |

## reload

While it runs, the gateway looks at its bundle files every `reload.intervalSeconds` and serves a new set of bundles without a restart, once the files are the same at two looks in a row. A set that fails its checks is refused with one warning, and the set in use stays. The configuration file itself is not read again.

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Limits | A change takes effect | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `reload` | section | no |  |  | at a restart | How the gateway looks for new bundles while it runs. |
| `reload.intervalSeconds` | whole number | no | `10` | 0 to 3600; 0 turns reloading off | at a restart | How often, in seconds, the bundle files and the certificate files are looked at. |

## tenants

The Community Edition serves one tenant (GWY008). The tenant name is the first segment of every address.

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Limits | A change takes effect | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `tenants` | section | yes |  | Community Edition: 1 tenant | at a restart | The tenants, by name. A name has lower-case letters, digits and -, starts with a letter or a digit, and is not health. |
| `tenants.<tenant>.bundles` | list of file or folder names | yes |  | at least one | at a restart | The bundles of the tenant, relative to the configuration file: a bundle file, or a folder whose *.rpgapi files are served, in name order. |
| `tenants.<tenant>.environments` | section | yes |  |  | at a restart | The environments of the tenant, by name, with the same rule for names as the tenants. |

## environments

The environment name is the second segment of every address. An environment with `backend: mock` needs nothing else. An environment with `backend: ibmi` needs JT400 (JTOpen), which the gateway does not include, and every key marked "with backend: ibmi"; those keys are refused with GWY002 in a `mock` environment. The Community Edition has one credential pair per tenant and environment.

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Limits | A change takes effect | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `tenants.<tenant>.environments.<environment>.code` | text | yes |  |  | at a restart | The code of the environment, which a bundle can pass to a program as ${environment.code}. |
| `tenants.<tenant>.environments.<environment>.backend` | mock or ibmi | yes |  |  | at a restart | mock answers from the mock definitions of the bundle; ibmi calls the programs on an IBM i. |
| `tenants.<tenant>.environments.<environment>.host` | text | with backend: ibmi |  | a host name or an address, without scheme, path or port | at a restart | The IBM i that the environment calls. |
| `tenants.<tenant>.environments.<environment>.libraryList` | list of library names | with backend: ibmi |  | 1 to 250 names of 1 to 10 characters | at a restart | The library list of the jobs that run the programs. |
| `tenants.<tenant>.environments.<environment>.credentials` | section | with backend: ibmi |  |  | at a restart | The sign-on of the environment. |
| `tenants.<tenant>.environments.<environment>.credentials.user` | placeholder | with backend: ibmi |  | a single ${NAME} | at a restart | The environment variable that holds the user. |
| `tenants.<tenant>.environments.<environment>.credentials.password` | placeholder | with backend: ibmi |  | a single ${NAME} | at a restart | The environment variable that holds the password. |
| `tenants.<tenant>.environments.<environment>.tls` | true or false | no | `true` |  | at a restart | Whether the connections to the IBM i use TLS. |
| `tenants.<tenant>.environments.<environment>.pool` | section | no |  |  | at a restart | The connections to the IBM i. |
| `tenants.<tenant>.environments.<environment>.pool.maxConnections` | whole number | no | `4` | 1 to 64 | at a restart | The most connections open at once to the IBM i. |
| `tenants.<tenant>.environments.<environment>.callTimeoutSeconds` | whole number | no | `30` | 1 to 3600 | at a restart | How long, in seconds, a call may take before it is given up. |

## Complete example

Every key, with a `mock` and an `ibmi` environment. The gateway starts with it, as a test of this repository checks, once `bundles/` holds a bundle, `tls/` holds the certificate and its encrypted key, and the environment variables are set.

<!-- snippet: reference/_notes/configuration/config.yaml -->
```yaml
# Every key of the gateway's configuration file. Started by ConfigurationExampleTest.
server:
  address: 0.0.0.0
  port: 8443
  tls:
    certificate: tls/tls.crt
    key: tls/tls.key
    keyPassword: ${TLS_KEY_PASSWORD}
management:
  address: 127.0.0.1
  port: 9090
reload:
  intervalSeconds: 10
tenants:
  acme:
    bundles:
      - ./bundles
    environments:
      test:
        code: T0001
        backend: mock
      prod:
        code: P0001
        backend: ibmi
        host: ${IBMI_HOST}
        libraryList: [APPLIB, QGPL]
        credentials:
          user: ${IBMI_USER}
          password: ${IBMI_PASSWORD}
        tls: true
        pool:
          maxConnections: 4
        callTimeoutSeconds: 30
```
